metadata.section: Section C: Labor Dynamics, Wages & Consumer Prices
metadata.visual_form: Animated Bar Race with Year Counter

events.label: Chip shortage: used car prices up 45%

explanation.summary: Inflation is an average of many prices. This chart takes it apart into six pieces of a household budget, so you can see which part drove prices up and when. The pandemic inflation hit in waves: used cars first, then gas, then groceries, and rent last.
explanation.methodology: Year-over-year change in six BLS Consumer Price Index categories (not seasonally adjusted): energy (CUUR0000SA0E), used cars and trucks (CUUR0000SETA02), food (CUUR0000SAF1), shelter (CUUR0000SAH1), transportation (CUUR0000SAT) and medical care (CUUR0000SAM).

key_findings.title: June 2021: Used Cars +45%
key_findings.description: A shortage of computer chips stopped new-car factories. Used car prices rose 45% in one year, the first wave of pandemic inflation.
key_findings.significance: One supply problem in one industry showed up in the national inflation number.

key_findings.title: June 2022: Energy +42%
key_findings.description: Energy prices were 41.6% higher than a year before. Food inflation followed, peaking at 11.4% in August 2022.
key_findings.significance: Energy feeds into almost every other price.

key_findings.title: March 2023: Rent Peaks Last
key_findings.description: Shelter inflation peaked at 8.2%, about nine months after energy. By then used car prices were falling (-11%).
key_findings.significance: Rents react slowly because leases last a year or more. As of August 2026, energy is up 16% again.
